1	# Growth — dedup local packs against the canon (per repo)
2	
3	The growth lifecycle's pruning stage: reconcile this repo's **local packs** against the shared **canon** it
4	consumes (Claudinite, vendored read-only), pruning local items — a pack's prose line, or a whole local check —
5	the canon now covers. It opens a PR against the repo's default branch for the owner to approve. Often there's
6	nothing to prune, and that's fine. You run under the executor, dispatched by a `ready-for-agent` issue; when
7	its Context names the newly-changed canon packs, focus the re-check there.
8	
9	> This task only prunes local packs against the canon; lifting local items up into the canon is the central
10	> promote task's job (canon-side).
11	
12	## Conventions used in this doc
13	
14	- **Default branch.** `main` stands for **this repository's default branch** — substitute whatever the repo uses.
15	- **GitHub access is MCP-native.** Updating the tracking issue and opening the PR go through the session's
16	  **GitHub MCP tools** (`mcp__github__*`). The unattended run has no shell GitHub access — the shell reaches
17	  only a git-over-HTTPS proxy scoped to one repo, with no REST credential — so never reach for `gh`/`curl` or
18	  a cross-repo clone.
19	- **The mounted canon.** The exact canon revision this repo currently consumes — compare against *that*, not a
20	  live fetch. It is what `.claudinite/shared/` holds at the mount's stamp (a promotion is visible here only
21	  once baselining has converged the mount to include it). Prune only against what the repo actually mounts.
22	- **The repo's local packs.** The set identified in [this pack's README](../../README.md#identifying-a-projects-capture-surface-its-local-packs) —
23	  everything under `.claudinite/local/packs/` (the legacy `.claudinite/local_packs/` accepted during the
24	  rename window). That's the corpus this task prunes within; the read-only mounted canon elsewhere under
25	  `.claudinite/` is never a prune target, only the yardstick you prune *against*.
26	
27	## What it does: prune / rephrase local packs the canon now covers
28	
29	When the canon has **absorbed** a practice a local doc still carries — most often an item the central promote
30	task lifted up and the canon now owns — the local copy is redundant. This task:
31	
32	- **Removes** the now-duplicated local item, since the canon is the single source of truth for portable rules.
33	- **Rephrases** a local procedure when the canon's wording of the same idea has changed, so the local packs
34	  stay consistent with the canon they point at.
35	
36	**Keep a local item only if it says *more* than the canon — not merely says it more specifically.** Every
37	local item is more specific than the canon, so specificity alone is never the test. Distinguish two cases:
38	
39	- **The general rule in local dress** — it makes the canon's point but leans on this repo's classes, files, or
40	  names to make it. Once the canon covers the point, those names were only illustration: prune it.
41	- **A stronger point about a narrower case** — it asserts something the canon's general rule leaves out: a
42	  tighter constraint, a sharper claim that holds for this repo's narrower situation. Keep it.
43	
44	So ask not "is it specific" (it always is) but "does it only lean on specific names to make the general point,
45	or does it make a point the canon doesn't?" Prune the first; keep the second.
46	
47	## A canon check covers an item too — and more strongly than prose
48	
49	The canon carries rules as **conformance checks**, not only prose. A local item is covered when a canon check
50	*enforces* it — stronger coverage than a stated line, since the rule runs on every session and CI pass.
51	Consult the machine-readable rule catalog (`node .claudinite/shared/engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs --list`:
52	id, severity, description, doc pointer — it lists the active local packs' own checks too) alongside the prose
53	corpus, and when a check covers the item, **quote the rule id** where you'd otherwise quote a canon line. This
54	cuts both ways: a **local pack's own check** is redundant once a canon check enforces the same rule — prune the
55	local `.mjs` (and drop it from `pack.mjs` + its fixture) exactly as you'd prune a duplicated prose line. The
56	keep-test above is unchanged: a local item that says *more* than the check detects (a stronger point about a
57	narrower case) stays.
58	
59	## Discipline
60	
61	- **Only remove a local item you can show the mounted canon genuinely covers — quote the canon line (or the
62	  covering check's rule id).** When unsure, leave it; a wrongful prune deletes a real local lesson.
63	- **Open a single PR against `main`** from a per-run-unique branch — one PR for the whole run's prunes, not one
64	  per item — never a direct push. This is an unattended task, on a capable model, and a **wrongful prune
65	  deletes a real local lesson**, so — unlike [growth-extract](../growth-extract/task.md), whose additive edits
66	  ride a PR that auto-merges after CI — this task keeps a **human** approval gate (its declared outcome ceiling
67	  is `open-pr`: it may open a PR but never merge it). **Put the issue reference in the commit message** —
68	  `Refs #<n>` for this task's tracking issue (below), in the commit itself, not only the PR body. The repo's
69	  `basics` `task-lifecycle` check gates a PR on its commits referencing an issue, so a prune commit that cites
70	  none reds the repo's CI and blocks the merge.
71	- If an edit touches something a test reads, run the repo's offline test suite and keep it green before pushing.
72	
73	## Tracking
74	
75	The task's standing log is the issue titled exactly, in this repo:
76	
77	> **Claudinite tracker: Growth Dedup**
78	
79	Find it **by that exact title, never a fuzzy match or a hard-coded number**. A run that finds no issue under
80	the exact title just creates one (closed). **Never open, close, or reopen it** afterward — its state carries no
81	meaning, only the log does. Log each run that changed a doc as a **dated comment** — naming what was pruned and
82	the canon line that now covers it. A run that prunes nothing logs nothing.
83	
84	## Run on a capable model
85	
86	Proving the mounted canon genuinely covers a local item before pruning it — and telling "the canon now owns
87	this" from "the canon states this too generally, keep the local cut" — is a **judgment call**. A downgraded
88	model prunes a real lesson; the review PR is a backstop, but a wrongful prune is easy to wave through in
89	review, so don't lean on it. This task declares `model: opus`; the executor dispatches its subagent there.
90	
91	## What this task must never do
92	
93	- **Never edit the read-only canon** — it only prunes the repo's *local packs* against it.
94	- **Never merge its own PR** — the human approval gate is the whole point (`outcome: open-pr`).
95	- **Never prune a local item without quoting the mounted-canon line (or covering check rule id) that covers
96	  it** — when unsure, leave it.
97	- **Never prune a local item that makes a stronger point about a narrower case** than the canon — that isn't
98	  redundancy. (A local item that only restates the canon in repo-specific names *is* prunable once the canon
99	  covers the point.)

{"number":648,"title":"Add a Claudinite conformance-checks job to CI (backstop for the Stop hook)","body":"## Problem

This repo runs the Claudinite conformance checks only via the **Stop hook** (Claude Code sessions). CI (`.github/workflows/test.yml`) does **not** run `node .claudinite/checks/run.mjs`, so a violation introduced outside a session — a human edit on GitHub web, or any non-session change — isn't caught by CI.

This surfaced during #646: the bespoke `shared-constants` uber test used to run inside `npm test` (so GCEC CI guarded those 8 constants on every PR). Retiring it in favor of Claudinite's canonical `shared-constants` check moved that enforcement to the Stop hook only. The canonical check is strictly better, but without a CI job it isn't a CI-level gate anymore.

## Fix

Add a CI job that runs the Claudinite check sweep (`node .claudinite/checks/run.mjs`) on PRs/pushes — the "CI is the backstop" job from Claudinite's design that this repo never picked up. It restores CI coverage for the migrated constants **and** adds it for every other Claudinite universal/tech-pack check (reference integrity, workflow lints, squash-merge history, etc.) — a net gain over the pre-#646 state.

Note the sequencing detail the check runner already documents: CI must ensure `.claudinite/` is populated (Method B tarball sync or submodule) before running the sweep.

{"number":438,"title":"Add a periodic "edge-case review" routine for the UI requirements","body":"A recurring (daily, Opus, Claude Code) routine that periodically re-reads `docs/uiRequirements.md` and the popup rendering code and **hunts for edge cases the requirements don't yet pin** — then either generates a `_(TBD)_` placeholder requirement (with a provisional snapshot of current behavior) for review, or, where the behavior is settled, generates the missing test. This is a thinking pass that should run regularly so gaps surface instead of accumulating silently.

### Why
This came out of a manual review pass that immediately turned up several uncovered/under-specified edge cases:
- **4.2.3** — cross-month grouping: one event with a Jun 15 instance, a Jun 28→Jul 3 *spanning* instance, and a Jul 10 instance. Today the span groups by its start (June only); should it also surface under July? (now a `_(TBD)_`).
- **4.10** — a single instance spanning multiple months: chip shows the start day only; should a long span show a date range on the calendar chip? (now a `_(TBD)_`).
- **5.7.3** — a grouped all-day card's header renders location-only; should it read "All day · location"? (now a `_(TBD)_`).
- **4.9** — the snapshot only checked card ordering, not within-card showing ordering (the second half of the requirement). Fixed this pass.
- **4.4** — "clickable" can't be shown by a cursor in the static renderer; a DOM assertion (the element is a `` whose computed `cursor` is `pointer`) belongs in a unit test. Candidate work item for this routine.

### Mechanics to mirror
Follow the existing daily-routine pattern (thin launcher pointing at an in-repo doc; its own standing tracking issue logging each run as dated comments; opens a PR, never merges) — see `docs/claude/auto-lessons.md`, `docs/claude/auto-fallback-coverage.md`, `docs/claude/auto-branch-report.md`. Add a daily unattended Claude **Opus** routine that tries to improve the **UI snapshot tests** — the counterpart of the existing daily routines (lessons `#365`, fallback-coverage `#366`, branch-report `#399`), each of which keeps its instructions in a repo doc and logs runs to its own standing tracking issue.

This routine runs **fully offline** on a fresh clone (the sandbox can't fetch live pages or run Chrome) and, like the others, **most days correctly changes nothing**.

## What it looks for

A genuinely useful, *true* improvement to the UI test suite, e.g.:

- **Claim accuracy** — a case that claims a requirement its snapshot can't actually verify (behavioral/unreachable leaves, the class found in the audit issue this references). Surface or re-home it.
- **Coverage honesty** — a leaf parked on a snapshot that should instead be a unit test on the view logic.
- **Missing rendering cases** — a leaf requirement whose visible rendering isn't actually pinned by any PNG, or a real rendering variation no case exercises.
- **Case simplification** — an over-complex case that could be split/trimmed per `docs/claude/testing.md` ("keep integration/UI cases as simple as possible").

## Scope / guardrails

- **Offline only**; deterministic. Touches `test/ui/**`, `ui/views/**` tests, and `docs/uiRequirements.md` claims — never ships popup behavior changes.
- An intentional pixel change must follow the **expected-vs-actual approval gate** (`docs/claude/workflow.md`) — never auto-accept a moved snapshot.
- Red-before-green; full suite green; regenerate `test/ui/README.md` via `npm run refresh:ui`.
- **PR for review, never a merge.** No real improvement → no branch, no PR.

## Plumbing (match the existing routines)

- New spec doc `docs/claude/auto-ui-tests.md`, imported from `CLAUDE.md`, written as the routine's source of truth; the launcher is a thin pointer to it (`docs/agenticBestPractices.md`).

1 # gcec rules 2 3 The project's standing working rules — injected at session start while this pack 4 is declared. Activity-scoped procedures live in this pack's skills 5 (snapshot-approval, merge-and-ci, testing-guide, add-live-case) and surface on 6 demand; the extractor-automation domain's standing rules are the "Extractor 7 pipeline" section below, and its two routines live under `dev/routines/`. 8 9 ## Working rules 10 11 - **Merges to `main` are squash, `(#N)` appended to the title** — a linear, 12 one-commit-per-PR history. CI must be green first (twice for e2e/heavy-browser 13 changes). The project mechanics of driving a merge (dispatching CI in a web 14 session, the poll back-off) are the merge-and-ci skill. 15 - **Generated files are regenerated, never hand-merged.** On a conflict take 16 either side and rerun `npm run regen` (load lists + UI snapshots + 17 fallback-coverage baseline/report). The committed `.gitattributes` maps each 18 generated file to the `ours` merge driver; a stale artifact can't slip through 19 — its own gate fails. Under the rule (kept in sync with `.gitattributes`): 20 `extension/event-extractors/load-order.generated.json` (from `npm run index`), 21 `dev/requirements//cases/*.png` (from `npm run refresh:ui`), and 22 `dev/requirements/extractor/fallback/fallback-coverage.baseline.GENERATED.json` 23 + `fallback-coverage.GENERATED.md` (from the fallback-coverage test). The 24 inline gallery in `dev/requirements/requirements.md` is part-authored prose — 25 **not** on the `ours` driver; reconcile via `npm run regen` + the gallery 26 drift gate. If `regen` reports a coverage regression, that's the real gate 27 firing — review it, don't paper over it. 28 - **One-time local git setup** (the cloud sandbox gets it from 29 `.claudinite/shared/engine/hooks/environment-setup-command.sh`): `git config rerere.enabled true` 30 and `git config merge.ours.driver true`. Without them nothing breaks — the 31 generated files just fall back to a manual conflicting merge. 32 - **Keep divergence small**: when starting work on a branch, `git merge 33 origin/main` (or rebase) **and run `npm run regen`** first, so the branch 34 carries freshly-generated artifacts, not just the latest sources. 35 - **Whenever a change regenerates the UI gallery** (via `npm run refresh:ui`), 36 link the branch's copy in the chat in the same turn you commit it — 37 `https://github.com///blob//dev/requirements/requirements.md` 38 — for one-page review. A moved snapshot baseline needs owner approval, never 39 silent regeneration: the process is the snapshot-approval skill. 40 41 ## Owner commands 42 43 - **"bump version"** = cut a release **end to end** — bump, merge, and wait for 44 the published artifact. Raise `version` in **both** `extension/manifest.json` 45 and `package.json` (kept identical by the `shared-constants` check), on a 46 branch. Default to a **minor** bump; honor an explicit target ("bump version 47 to 1.4.0") or level ("bump patch" / "bump major") when given. Open the PR, 48 get CI green, squash-merge with `(#N)` — 49 saying "bump version" is itself the merge authorization for **this** 50 deterministic bump PR only. The merge triggers **Release: Create Package**; 51 do **not** report done until the `vX.Y.Z` GitHub Release with its refreshed 52 `google-calendar-event-creator.zip` asset is published — poll via the GitHub 53 MCP tools on the merge-and-ci skill's back-off (reporting at merge time races 54 the async build). 55 - **"learned lessons"** = run the canon lessons-learned pass over the current 56 conversation on **the strongest model available**, plus the standing 57 efficiency analysis of the conversation's tool/process usage. Only when the 58 owner asks — never extract unprompted. Capture routing: see below. 59 60 ## Testing invariants 61 62 - `npm test` runs everything; `test:live` (reviewed integration cases against 63 cached pages), `test:offline` (unit), `test:ui` (popup/icon snapshots), 64 `refresh:ui` (regenerate after an intentional UI change), `test:e2e` (heavy, 65 CI-only). The suites, harnesses, and requirements model are mapped in the 66 testing-guide skill. 67 - **Integration cases are the reviewed contract** — a person reads 68 `dev/requirements/extractor/expected/`; nobody reviews the unit tests. Every 69 required change or bugfix gets a case (one real, focused page per distinct 70 behavior; keep cases minimal). Unit tests under `extension-test/` are a 71 supplementary safety net for page-independent logic. 72 - **`extension-test/` mirrors `extension/`'s tree, one test per source file** 73 (`extension//.js` → `extension-test//.test.js`; the 74 path IS the link, so a source file never names its test). Deliberate 75 departures: `extension-test/integration/` for whole-extension/interaction 76 tests; no mirror for `custom/*` sources or data/markup files (covered by live 77 cases / snapshots / drift guards); `extension-test/harness.js` is shared 78 infra (not a test) and stays at the root. The hand-kept `test:offline` list in 79 `package.json` is enforced against the tree by this pack's 80 `test-offline-list-sync` check. 81 - **Requirement tests render against the pinned `REFERENCE_NOW`** 82 (`dev/requirements/shared/reference-time.js`, currently 2026-06-01), never the 83 wall clock. The pinned day is the floor of the cases' dates: author a 84 neutral/upcoming case **on or after it** so it's pill-free; use a past date or 85 a future year only when the case is *pinning* a pill. 86 87 ## Codebase gotchas 88 89 Project-wide footguns only — a trap you'd only hit *while editing one specific 90 file* belongs in that file's top-of-file header comment (see the capture policy 91 below). Portable rules these instantiate live in the canon packs/skills. 92 93 - **`declarativeContent`/`UrlFilter` host-match verification is CI-only** — the 94 lookalike-`hostSuffix` gotcha and the `hostEquals` + dot-`hostSuffix` 95 apex-or-subdomain fix are the canon `chrome-extension` pack's; the real 96 URL→icon match runs inside Chrome, exercised here only by the CI-only 97 real-Chrome test (`dev/requirements/heavy/extension-load.chrome.test.js`). 98 - **CDP-introspecting the MV3 worker hits the portable traps** (canon): here 99 they bit `declarativeContent…getRules` (hung until job timeout), which is why 100 the awaited signal is built from plain promises and the worker publishes 101 `globalThis.iconRulesReady` for the test to poll. Bound every probe and add a 102 test-level timeout regardless. 103 - **The jsdom-vs-Chrome DOM traps bit this repo directly** (canon): #130/#137 104 drove the **production** remedy the canon (framed for tests) leaves out — 105 strip `noscript`/`script`/`style` from a clone before reading any element's 106 user-facing text (the fallback's footer-address reader does this, #675). 107 - **Injected block markup inside a `

` silently empties it** — the parser 108 auto-closes the `

` and the content lands as its `nextElementSibling`; a 109 `.foo p` selector reads `""` with no error. Bit tel-aviv's description blocks 110 (#602) — read the sibling, not the tag. 111 - **The augment-not-replace + reset-per-load rule lands on `GCal` here** 112 (canon): `registry.js` resets `GCal.sources` on load and is pinned **first** 113 in the load order so it runs before any source pushes (#48, #189). 114 - **`clean()` collapses all whitespace including newlines — single-line fields 115 only.** A description run through it loses every line break (#131, #140, 116 #141); multi-line text goes through the block helpers (`blockText` / 117 `normalizeBlock` / `htmlToText`). Line-break handling is generic, never a 118 per-source choice. 119 - **A supported/registered host is necessary but not sufficient for "an 120 event"** — gating on `Boolean(site)` surfaced phantom events on home pages 121 (#133); a real event requires actual data (JSON-LD or a parsed date), never a 122 mere host match. 123 - **The vendored `.claudinite/shared` canon reflects its stamp, not canon 124 `main`** — check the `claudinite` stamp in `.claudinite-checks.json` (and 125 whether the nightly refresh has run since an upstream fix merged) **before** 126 concluding an upstream fix hasn't arrived and **before committing a 127 workaround for a check finding** (an accept, a suppression pragma): a stale 128 canon twice produced spurious findings whose fixes had already merged 129 (#664, #665). 130 - **The cloud Setup script runs as root starting in the repo's parent dir**, 131 not the checkout — a bare `npm ci` there silently installs nothing; 132 `.claudinite/shared/engine/hooks/environment-setup-command.sh` `cd`s into the checkout first 133 (#186/#196). 134 135 ## Workflow-failure classification 136 137 An unattended workflow must converge its failure to a human-visible state (the 138 rule and the `report-failure` reporter live in the canon). This repo's 139 classification: the `Release` stub (`chrome-extension-release.yml`) is 140 unattended and already covered — the reporters fire inside the vendored 141 create-package/publish/daily workflows, keyed per operation, with per-repo 142 values in `.github/release.config`; `test.yml` is attended PR CI — no reporter; 143 `fetch-page.yml` is attended by its dispatcher (see the extractor pipeline 144 section below); a **new** unattended workflow adds a failure job per the canon 145 action header's recipe. 146 147 ## Extractor pipeline 148 149 Standing rules for the extractor-automation domain — the create-extractor routine 150 (an `extractor-request` issue → a PR adding site support), still under 151 [`dev/routines/`](../../../../dev/routines/), and the weekly 152 fallback-extractor-improvements task, now a gcec pack task under 153 [`tasks/`](tasks/fallback-extractor-improvements/) (read a spec only when working 154 on that pipeline). Adding a cached live case is the 155 [add-live-case](skills/add-live-case/SKILL.md) skill. 156 157 - **All page fetching is delegated to ScraperAPI via the fetch-page workflow** 158 (`.github/workflows/fetch-page.yml`): a bare curl through ScraperAPI's 159 residential proxy with `render=true`, so a single-page app records post-render 160 HTML with real data. Bot-blocking from CI/sandbox IPs is the portable rule 161 maintained in the canon; here the escape hatch is the `SCRAPER_API_KEY` 162 **GitHub Actions secret** — a page is recorded by dispatching that workflow (the 163 create-extractor routine does this in its step 4), never by a local fetch (this 164 sandbox is bot-blocked). ScraperAPI is the whole fetching surface — swap the 165 vendor in that one workflow if it underperforms. The aid for a flaky SPA render 166 is the **`Wait-for selector`** a source request can carry 167 (`extension/events-popup/derive-wait-selector.js`, a source-request tool, NOT an 168 event extractor, #603), passed to the workflow as `wait_for_selector`. 169 - **Facebook can't be a cached live case** — a hard HTTP 400 even through the 170 proxy, so its extraction stays unit-tests-only 171 (`extension-test/event-extractors/extraction.test.js`). 172 - **Rendered output isn't deterministic.** A re-record can legitimately shift a 173 live case's `expected` — treat such drift like a site-markup change, and prefer 174 extracting JSON-LD/`og:` (which apps still inject) over brittle DOM positions. 175 - **An ambiguous numeric slash date is read by the page's declared locale, 176 centrally — never per-source, never guessed.** `"05/07/2026"` (both parts ≤ 12) 177 reads month-first by default (V8's US convention) and flips day-first only on a 178 *positive* non-US signal — an explicit non-US region in `` / 179 `og:locale`, or a non-English language; a bare `en` (region unknown) stays 180 month-first rather than guess. Resolution lives in `helpers/dates.js` 181 (`parseDateFromText` / `normalizeDateValue` take a `dayFirst` flag, threaded 182 from `extract-unsupported.js`'s `pageUsesDayFirstDates`), mirroring 183 `derive-timezone.js`'s locale read; unambiguous dates (a part > 12) and the 184 `.` / `-` separators are always day-first regardless (#686). 185 - **`fetch-page.yml` is attended by its dispatcher** (the workflow-failure 186 classification above): the create-extractor routine dispatches it, polls the 187 run, and on failure labels the issue `extractor-blocked-needs-human` — a red run 188 reaches a human through the routine, not the Actions list, so the workflow 189 carries no failure reporter (and being dispatch-only it never runs unwatched). 190 - **The fallback-coverage gate is a high-watermark over a changing case set.** It 191 ratchets up on an unchanged case set and re-anchors when the set changes, 192 compared over the cases the runs **share** — so adding an extractor never fails 193 it (#240) while a pre-existing case that regresses still does. A removed/renamed 194 case the watermark still lists makes it stale: the local refresh re-anchors it 195 (commit that); in CI it's an error to fix. *Caveat:* never commit a re-anchored 196 baseline while the gate is red — a regression bundled with a case-set change can 197 be re-anchored over. Detailed mechanics self-document in the gate's own headers 198 (`dev/requirements/extractor/fallback/fallback-coverage.js` / `.test.js`). 199 - **To see what the generic/unsupported extractor gets** on any cached page — even 200 a supported host — load the files, set `GCal.sources = []`, then call 201 `GCal.extract()`: the documented way to force the unsupported-host path through 202 the same norm/sort the popup uses. Most start/end *differences* vs a dedicated 203 source are just its hardcoded `ctz` localizing to floating time (same instant), 204 not extraction bugs; the real gaps are fields it can't know generically 205 (durations, site-specific descriptions, and — where the page doesn't declare 206 corroborating hints, see `helpers/derive-timezone.js` — `ctz`). This is the 207 comparison the fallback-coverage gate automates. 208 209 ## Architecture rules of the road 210 211 Whenever we agree on a new or changed top-level architectural guideline, update 212 this section as part of the same change (the design doc itself is 213 `dev/procedures/highLevelDesign.md`): 214 215 - Adding support for a new host is the most common change — the architecture 216 must keep it a single, self-contained new file 217 (`extension/event-extractors/custom/.js`) plus regenerating the load 218 list, touching nothing else and assuming nothing about other extractors. 219 220 ## Capture policy — lessons land in the local packs 221 222 **The gcec local pack is this repo's capture surface.** Route each lesson to its 223 section here (extractor-automation to the "Extractor pipeline" section, 224 everything else to the fitting section) — then pick the *mechanism* before 225 writing prose (the canon promotion ladder, applied locally): a check in the 226 pack's `rules` beats prose every time (`test-offline-list-sync` is the worked 227 example — a 228 testable sentence became a rule module with red-first fixtures); an 229 activity-scoped procedure becomes a pack skill; only what neither can carry 230 lands in RULES.md, terse. 231 232 - **File-local footguns go in the file, not here.** A trap you'd only trip 233 *while editing one specific file* (a mistake of **commission**, made with the 234 file open) belongs in that file's top-of-file header comment — on-demand 235 context, can't drift, off the always-loaded budget. Keep it central here only 236 when Claude could hit it *without* reading the locus file (a mistake of 237 **omission**, or a cross-cutting invariant). One file can split both ways: 238 the jsdom traps stay here (generic extraction hits them without reading the 239 harness) while `extension-test/harness.js`'s own parsing mechanics live in 240 its header. 241 - **Portable lessons are captured here too** — locally, in the owning pack, 242 exactly like project-specific ones. Portability is the Claudinite canon's 243 concern (its growth routine generalizes local packs into shared canon and 244 prunes what the canon comes to cover); never edit the read-only mount or 245 reach across to Claudinite from here. 246 - Keep every addition terse; dedupe against the canon before adding. 247

Some sites emit the venue's whole formatted postal address as the schema.org
Place.name ("Museum, Kaplan St, Tel Aviv-Yafo, Israel") AND repeat the pieces
in the structured `address`. The generic fallback's location composer then
re-appended the parsed street/region on top of the name, producing a duplicated,
noisier string than the dedicated source (which reads the name as-is).

When Place.name already contains BOTH the city (addressLocality) and the street
core (streetAddress minus its house number), treat it as a complete formatted
address and use it verbatim, skipping the structured parts. Requiring both the
city and a substantive street core keeps a venue merely named after its city
("Zappa Tel Aviv", street elsewhere) from qualifying, so its street is still
composed in.

Generic (keys off the schema.org full-formatted-name convention, not a host).
Lifts the eventer.co.il fallback location from a diff to an exact match; no
other corpus case changes. Fallback-coverage: criticalFieldsPct 73.5->74.3,
allFieldsPct 54->54.4.

* gcec: add agent_execution_timeout to fallback-extractor-improvements

Convert the one gcec pack task to the agent-preprocessing contract
(Claudinite agent-preprocessing DESIGN §2, §6): an agentic task
(agent_model !== 'none') must declare a positive-integer
agent_execution_timeout — the best-effort run bound the executor
surfaces into the subagent's brief as "fail after N minutes".

Set generously (5400s / 90 min): this is an open-ended judgment loop
(hypothesize -> edit -> the network-bound test:live -> compare,
iterated), so the bound is extreme runaway protection, not a scheduling
knob. No deterministic pre-step is split into agent_preprocessing here —
the baseline the agent picks targets from is measured on a fresh clone
and must be seen by the agent, and preprocessing has no code->agent data
channel (DESIGN §3), so the task stays a single agentic stage. (The
fetch/scaffold pre-step the design notes belongs to the create-extractor
pipeline, still a legacy dev/routines/ routine outside tasks/.)

Server-side templating that drops a multi-line description straight into a
schema.org "description" emits RAW (unescaped) newlines inside the JSON string.
That is invalid JSON, so a strict JSON.parse() throws and embeddedEvents.find()
silently discards an otherwise-perfectly-good Event — the page's strongest
machine-readable signal — leaving the generic fallback to guess from body text.
Seen on ASP.NET/SharePoint and hand-built CMSes (visit.tel-aviv.gov.il is the
corpus example; its own custom source documents having to bypass the broken
JSON-LD entirely).

On a parse failure, escape only the control characters that appear INSIDE string
literals and retry once. This rewrites nothing structural — control chars
between tokens are already valid whitespace and are left byte-for-byte
untouched — and never fabricates data; if the salvaged text still won't parse,
the block is dropped as before.

Generic (keys off the schema.org JSON-LD convention, not a host) and Chrome-safe
(a typed <script type="application/ld+json"> is read via .textContent, which
Chrome exposes identically to jsdom — not the innerText/body-text trap; the
recovered start/end/description are all present in the page's visible DOM too).
Lifts visit-tel-aviv-timed's fallback start (~->exact), end (missing->exact) and
description (~->exact). Fallback-coverage: criticalFieldsPct 74.3->75.2,
allFieldsPct 54.4->55.9; no other corpus case changes.

./packs/git-github/skills/git-github-advanced/SKILL.md:25:- **One caveat, at merge time: before rebasing an *unmerged* multi-commit branch onto a *moved* base, collapse commits that rewrite the same lines into one.** When your own commits churn the same lines (build X → refactor → remove X, common in an iterative design session) and the base has advanced, rebasing the stack replays *every* intermediate conflict against the new base. The squash-merge discards those commits anyway, so collapse them first — `git reset --soft $(git merge-base HEAD origin/main)` then one fresh commit, and rebase that single commit: one conflict pass, not N. ./packs/git-github/skills/git-github-advanced/SKILL.md:28:- After your commit is **squash-merged** to `main`, a *reused* feature branch still carries that original commit (the squash created a *new* commit on `main`, so the branch's own is unreachable from it) — and the next PR off the branch re-includes it in the diff, because the three-dot merge-base predates the squash. 1	---
2	name: merge-to-main
3	description: Merge the change in front of the owner into main. Use when the owner says "LGTM" or asks to merge/land the current branch or PR into main.
4	---
5	
6	
7	The portable recipe for landing the change in front of the owner on `main` — the *mechanics* behind the owner's merge-to-main command (the owner's preferences own the trigger *phrase*; this file owns the *how*). Invoked through the `merge-to-main` skill (this skill); this doc stays the canonical recipe.
8	
9	**A project's bespoke merge policy overrides this default.** Most projects need nothing here — this default is the whole story. A project that genuinely diverges (a different merge method, a CI/twice-green gate, an extra approval) **states so by naming its merge-policy file explicitly in its own `CLAUDE.md`**. When that declaration is present, read that file first and let it override the divergent points below; when it's absent, follow this default as-is. Don't go hunting for a policy file that the project's `CLAUDE.md` doesn't name.
10	
11	## Recipe (~4 calls)
12	
13	1. Load both GitHub tools in **one** `ToolSearch`: `create_pull_request` + `merge_pull_request`.
14	2. No PR open for the branch yet? `create_pull_request` (base `main`); end the body with `Closes #<issue>`, and take the PR number from the returned URL.
15	3. Gate on CI **only if the repo has it** — a workflow that actually runs on PRs/pushes. `workflow_call`-only reusable workflows (this repo hosts some) are *not* CI: they never run here, so a non-empty `.github/workflows/` alone proves nothing; check the PR for check runs instead. No CI → no gate; don't wait for checks that will never come.
16	4. `merge_pull_request`, `merge_method: squash`, title `<subject> (#<pr>)`. Merge directly — don't pre-read status; the call fails loudly if it isn't mergeable.
17	5. Sync local `main`: `git checkout main && git pull origin main`.
18	
19	The two divergent points — **`squash`** as the method and **CI gating** — are exactly what a bespoke policy file changes.
20	
21	## After the merge: capture the conversation (every session, every user)
22	
23	Once the merge has landed and local `main` is synced, run the growth pack's capture step:
24	`node .claudinite/shared/packs/grow_with_claudinite/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>` (from the canon repo itself: `node packs/grow_with_claudinite/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`), `<n>` being the issue your `Closes #<issue>` named. Deterministic, seconds-long; it pushes the conversation to the orphan `conversation-logs` branch. It runs **here, in-session, because it needs the live transcript** — the lessons extraction then happens later in the fleet's `conversation-extract` run_daily task (central, MCP-native, with a rethink window), so there is nothing to schedule and no in-session lessons pass ([the pack README](../../../../packs/grow_with_claudinite/README.md) owns the standard). A later merge in the same session just runs capture again — it captures the delta. In the rare repo that removed the `grow_with_claudinite` pack from `.claudinite-checks.json`, skip this step.
25	
26	## Don't
27	
28	- **Don't** re-read the issue to confirm it closed — `Closes #<issue>` does that on merge; trust it.
29

1	---
2	name: merge-and-ci
3	description: Drive this repo's PR-to-merged flow cheaply — when to open the PR, how to get CI green in a Claude web session, and how to poll without wasting wall time or tokens. Use when merging a change, waiting on CI, or opening a PR that touches e2e/heavy/UI tests.
4	---
5	
6	# Merge and CI in this repo
7	
8	The merge itself: squash, `(#N)` appended to the title, CI green first (twice
9	for e2e/heavy-browser changes), approval-applies-only-backward — see the gcec
10	pack's RULES.md. This skill is the *how*: the environment facts and the poll
11	discipline that keep a merge cheap in wall time and tokens (from a post-mortem
12	on treating CI as a fixed poll-and-sleep ritual).
13	
14	## Open the PR early when the only reviewable output is on CI
15	
16	A change that adds or modifies an e2e/heavy-browser (`dev/requirements/heavy/`)
17	or UI-snapshot (`dev/requirements/{popup,icon}/`) test can't be exercised
18	locally — the sandbox has no Chrome — and its reviewable artifacts only exist
19	on a PR: CI runs the heavy/e2e suites against the branch, and a UI change's
20	reviewable output (the pixel diff GitHub renders, the inline gallery in the
21	branch's `dev/requirements/requirements.md`) needs a pushed branch to view at
22	all. Open the PR early for those.
23	
24	## Getting a green check in a Claude web session
25	
26	- **The push-run exists — don't dispatch a duplicate.** A push through the
27	  in-session git proxy **does** trigger `test.yml`: the workflow's `push`
28	  trigger covers `main` and `claude/**` precisely so an agent branch gets CI
29	  without a PR, and a branch that also has an open PR gets a `pull_request` run
30	  too (two `test` check runs on the same head SHA — the workflow's own comment
31	  calls that accepted duplication). Merge on whichever is green; only reach for
32	  `actions_run_trigger` / `run_workflow` when no run appeared at all (a branch
33	  outside `claude/**`, or a `paths-ignore`/`[skip ci]` push). Firing a manual
34	  dispatch on top of a run that already exists just buys a third run and its
35	  wall time.
36	- **The shell can't observe GitHub state here.** The git remote is a git-only
37	  proxy (smart-HTTP under `/git/<owner>/<repo>/…`; every other path 400s),
38	  there's no API token in the env, and `gh` reaches no `api.github.com` — only
39	  an MCP poll sees check state; a background bash/Monitor loop cannot.
40	- **Poll `get_check_runs`, never `get_status`.** `pull_request_read`'s
41	  `get_status` reads the legacy commit-status API, which nothing in this repo
42	  writes — it returns `state: "pending"`, `total_count: 0` forever, including
43	  long after every check run has finished green. Trusting it means waiting on a
44	  transition that never comes. CI here is GitHub Actions **check runs**, so
45	  `get_check_runs` is the only reading of "is CI green" that is ever true.
46	- **Poll on a short back-off, never one long sleep, never tight.** Loop
47	  **MCP poll → background sleep → MCP poll** until the check leaves
48	  `in_progress`, backing off **5s, 10s, 15s, 30s, then 30s** repeating — a
49	  fast run wakes you within seconds, a slow one isn't tight-polled. Always wait
50	  for the sleep's completion notification before the next poll. While a sleep
51	  runs, do real work (review the diff, draft the PR body) or end the turn —
52	  filler calls to look busy are tight-polling in disguise.
53	- **Don't reach for `subscribe_pr_activity` to wait for green** — its webhooks
54	  never deliver CI **success** (only failures/comments/reviews), so the
55	  transition you're waiting for never arrives. It's for babysitting a PR, not
56	  merge-on-green.
57	- **Batch tool loading**: one `ToolSearch` for every GitHub MCP tool the flow
58	  needs (`issue_write`, `create_pull_request`, `pull_request_read`,
59	  `merge_pull_request`), not one per turn.
60

1	# Fallback-coverage routine
2	
3	Weekly Claude routine (on a strong model), offline on a fresh clone. Goal: make the **generic**
4	fallback extractor — `extension/event-extractors/extract-unsupported.js` and the
5	shared `extension/event-extractors/helpers/*.js` — recover **more** of what the
6	dedicated per-site sources get, measured by the fallback-coverage gate. **Most runs
7	correctly change nothing** — the gate already banks every prior win, so a new
8	generic win is rare and a forced or fake one is worse than none. No win → no branch,
9	no PR.
10	
11	## 1. Scope — the strong model runs only because the cheap gate already passed
12	
13	This task is a two-tier run, cheap gate first: the **scheduler** (a pure-code Action,
14	no model at all) ran this task's precondition (`task.mjs`, over the `commits` signal),
15	and only *because* it found a meaningful change did it dispatch you — a strong-model
16	subagent — via the `ready-for-agent` issue. Most weeks the gate skips and no strong
17	model ever boots; you are paid for solely on the weeks there's real work. (This is
18	the "cheap dispatcher front door" cost model — the scheduler precondition is that
19	front door, cheaper than a dispatcher session because it runs no model.)
20	
21	So **you don't re-run that gate.** The dispatch issue's **Context** names the
22	substantive commits in the window; treat it as binding scope and don't re-litigate
23	whether to run. Still: **most runs correctly change nothing** (below), so "ran" never
24	means "must produce a PR".
25	
26	## 2. Measure the baseline
27	
28	```sh
29	npm install && npm run test:live
30	```
31	
32	The gate prints a "fallback value differences (informational)" block and a
33	per-exemplar matrix (✓ match · ~ different value · ✗ missing · — n/a): a `~` is a
34	concrete generic gap the fallback gets wrong, a `✗` a field it finds nothing for —
35	your candidate targets. This run is your pre-change reference (the committed
36	`fallback-coverage.baseline.GENERATED.json`); don't `git stash`/rerun to re-derive
37	it — that conflicts on the `ours`-driver GENERATED artifacts. A committed baseline
38	listing **fewer** `cases` than the live run is pre-existing drift, not something
39	your change introduced. Gate mechanics: [the gcec pack’s RULES.md](../../RULES.md)
40	(and the gate's own headers).
41	
42	## 3. Improve — the feedback loop
43	
44	Pick one or a few `~`/`✗` gaps and close them, iterating: **hypothesize → edit only
45	the generic extractor / helpers → `npm run test:live` → compare to the baseline**,
46	until you have one or more clean wins (or conclude there are none). Every change
47	must clear the bars **postconditions.sh** enforces in step 4 — hold to them as you
48	work, because a run that trips one there is marked **failed**:
49	
50	- **Generic only** (postcondition: *scope*). Key off a widely-used convention that
51	  would help unseen sites — display conventions (date↔time separators, start–end
52	  ranges, "Event @ Venue" titles, ordinals) or machine-readable signals (schema.org
53	  JSON-LD, OG/meta, microdata, `<time datetime>`). Lifting one `custom/<site>.js`'s
54	  logic or special-casing a host is out of scope: if the only beneficiary is a
55	  single case and the rule wouldn't fire elsewhere, it isn't generic. **The only
56	  files you may leave changed are `extract-unsupported.js`, `helpers/*.js`, your
57	  covering test in `extension-test/event-extractors/extraction.test.js`, and the
58	  regenerated fallback-coverage GENERATED artifacts** — anything else fails scope.
59	- **A real, non-regressing win** (postcondition: *win*, via the suite's gate). Every
60	  gated % must end **≥** its baseline and at least one strictly higher; a change
61	  that lifts one field but drops another isn't clean — drop it.
62	- **No illusory win** (postcondition: *jsdom*). The offline body-text scan reads
63	  `document.body.textContent`, which includes `<script>` JSON (Next.js
64	  `__NEXT_DATA__`), `<noscript>`, `<style>`, `<select>/<option>`, and CSS-hidden
65	  text — none of which Chrome's `innerText` exposes. A win matching only such
66	  content is illusory; a real one comes from visible text or a Chrome-read attribute
67	  (meta / JSON-LD / microdata / `<time datetime>`). **In step 4 you must pass every
68	  value the change newly recovered via the body-text scan** so this is checked.
69	  (Widening a scan-window cap can make a *different* case match a `<script>` blob it
70	  never reached — re-run the whole corpus before raising any cap.)
71	- **No forbidden win.** Don't invent `ctz` or `eventLengthInMinutes` (a wrong `ctz`
72	  is worse than none). `ctz` may only be *derived*, never guessed: two independent
73	  page-declared hints must agree — the contract
74	  `extension/event-extractors/helpers/derive-timezone.js` implements (#674/#676) —
75	  so never weaken its refusal rules for a coverage win. When a change fills a field
76	  generically, also check the cases whose dedicated source deliberately leaves that
77	  field EMPTY (stubhub/seetickets set no `ctz`) still come out empty — a "win"
78	  there silently breaks strict parity. `start`/`end` already match when they
79	  resolve to the same instant, so don't chase representation-only differences;
80	  never override a miss a unit test deliberately asserts.
81	- **Covered and clean.** Add or extend a case in
82	  `extension-test/event-extractors/extraction.test.js`, red-before-green; the full
83	  `npm test` must be green (postcondition: *suite*). Never weaken a test, lower the
84	  gate, or hand-edit a GENERATED file — commit the regenerated baseline + scorecard
85	  as produced.
86	
87	If no clean generic win emerges, print `No generic fallback-coverage improvement found.`
88	and stop.
89	
90	## 4. Postcondition
91	
92	Pass every value the change newly recovered via the body-text scan as arguments:
93	
94	```sh
95	bash .claudinite/local/packs/gcec/tasks/fallback-extractor-improvements/postconditions.sh "<recovered value>" ...
96	```
97	
98	- Exit 0 → the win is valid; go to step 5.
99	- **Non-zero → the run has FAILED.** Do not retry and do not open a PR; surface the
100	  failure so guiding prose can be re-introduced to this routine.
101	
102	## 5. Open the PR (never merge)
103	
104	Branch `claude/fallback-coverage/<date>`, commit the change plus the regenerated
105	GENERATED artifacts, and push. Then open a **PR for review** — it never merges
106	itself; from there it goes through the usual flow (the gcec pack's
107	[merge-and-ci skill](../../skills/merge-and-ci/SKILL.md)), and CI must
108	go green **twice** (it touches `test:live`). PR body: the hypothesis, why it's generic (which unseen sites
109	it helps), how the jsdom trap was ruled out, the before→after numbers, and the
110	covering test.
111	
112	Then log the run as a dated comment (**not** a sub-issue) on the standing
113	*Auto-Improvements Tracker - Fallback Extractor Coverage* issue (find it **by
114	title**, currently #366; open it if missing, reopen it if closed) so it builds a
115	scrollable history, and `Refs` that issue in the PR.

  # Manual runs from the Actions tab / API, on any branch. GitHub only exposes
  # this once the workflow is on the default branch, so it covers future dev
  # branches; for a brand-new branch, the push trigger below runs CI right away.
  workflow_dispatch:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  push:
    # main, plus agent dev branches, so CI (including the real-Chrome e2e smoke
    # test) runs on a dev branch without opening a PR. A branch that also has an
    # open PR gets a pull_request run too — accepted as minor duplication.
    branches: [main, "claude/**"]
    # Pushes from the "Fetch cached page" workflow (fetch-page.yml) only touch
    # dev/requirements/extractor/data/ and carry [skip ci]; this is a redundant extra guard against
    # re-triggering this workflow. (UI snapshots have no fetch workflow — they're
    # regenerated by hand — so a commit that changes them SHOULD run CI to validate
    # them.)
    paths-ignore:
      - "dev/requirements/extractor/data/**"

# GitHub's implicit run shell is bash -e without pipefail, so a failing piped
# command still shows the step green. Force pipefail for every run: step.
defaults:
  run:
    shell: bash

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Validate extension manifest.json
        run: node -e "JSON.parse(require('fs').readFileSync('extension/manifest.json'))"

      # "For me" tests: deterministic, no network. These gate every change.
      - name: Run offline tests
        run: npm run test:offline

      # "For you" tests: the reviewed assertions, run against the cached
      # HTML files committed to dev/requirements/extractor/data/ (recorded by the "Fetch cached page"
      # workflow, fetch-page.yml — this job does not fetch them).
      - name: Run live tests
        run: npm run test:live

      # Renders each dev/requirements/<kind>/cases/*.case.js through the popup's real render() and
      # compares it to the committed dev/requirements/<kind>/cases/*.png (browsable on GitHub).
      # Deterministic and dependency-light (satori + resvg, no browser), so it
      # runs alongside the other tests.
      - name: Run UI snapshot test
        run: npm run test:ui

      # Real-Chrome smoke test: loads the unpacked extension and asserts the MV3
      # service worker registers — the one layer that exercises Chrome's actual
      # extension loader, the layer that broke in #146. The test itself has no
      # npm dependency (it drives Chrome over the DevTools Protocol via Node's
      # built-in WebSocket). Two environment quirks handled here:
      #   * branded Chrome 137+ dropped the --load-extension switch, so we fetch
      #     Chrome for Testing via `npx @puppeteer/browsers` (run on demand, not
      #     a project dependency — nothing added to package.json/the lockfile);
      #   * MV3 extensions only load in *headful* Chrome, so it runs under xvfb.
      # Separate from the browserless suites above; the test skips if no Chrome.
      #
      # The Chrome for Testing download (~150 MB) is cached to keep CI fast. The
      # key rolls monthly so the cache is reused on virtually every run, while
      # still refreshing to a current Chrome often enough to catch Chrome changes
      # (the whole point of this layer).
      - name: Chrome for Testing cache key
        id: cft-key
        run: echo "key=cft-${{ runner.os }}-$(date -u +%Y-%m)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - name: Cache Chrome for Testing
        uses: actions/cache@v6
        with:
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/cft
          key: ${{ steps.cft-key.outputs.key }}
      - name: Run real-Chrome extension-load smoke test
        run: |
          # Reuse the cached binary when present; otherwise fetch Chrome for Testing.
          CHROME_PATH="$(find "${RUNNER_TEMP}/cft" -type f -name chrome 2>/dev/null | head -n1)"
          if [ -z "$CHROME_PATH" ]; then
            out="$(npx --yes @puppeteer/browsers install chrome@stable --path "${RUNNER_TEMP}/cft")"
            echo "$out"
            CHROME_PATH="$(echo "$out" | tail -n1 | awk '{print $NF}')"
          fi
          export CHROME_PATH
          echo "Using Chrome at: $CHROME_PATH"
          xvfb-run --auto-servernum npm run test:e2e

content.content:
---
name: snapshot-approval
description: Get owner approval for a moved UI-snapshot baseline. Use whenever a change to a dev/requirements case (its spec or its rendering) makes the snapshot tests fail — the pixels moved and the baseline wants to change.
---

# Snapshot-approval process

The general principle — a moved snapshot/golden baseline needs owner approval,
not silent regeneration — is canon. This is the project process when a change
to a `dev/requirements/<kind>/cases/*` case makes the snapshot tests **fail**:

1. **Surface the diff immediately, don't carry on.** Revert the baseline to the
   committed **expected** PNG, run the snapshot test so it fails (the harness
   writes the rendered `actual` and a highlighted `diff` to
   `dev/requirements/shared/.artifacts/`), and send three images to the chat:
   **expected** (committed), **actual** (newly-rendered), and the **diff**.
   When the change alters the PNG's **dimensions** (e.g. a fixture shrink),
   pixelmatch can't diff unequal sizes so the harness writes only `actual` (no
   `diff`) — stitch **expected** and **actual** side-by-side into one image for
   the review instead.
2. **Ask via `AskUserQuestion`, not prose** — a popup notifies the owner on
   mobile. Offer **Approve** and **Reject — let's discuss**.
3. **Hold without overwriting the expected image.** If the working tree must be
   committed while waiting (e.g. a stop-hook), commit the *reverted* (expected)
   baseline so the branch/PR honestly shows the snapshot test **red, pending
   approval** — never commit the new baseline first.
4. On **Approve**: regenerate the baseline (`npm run refresh:ui`), confirm the
   suite is green, and push. On **Reject**: **do not** roll back automatically —
   leave the change in place and discuss how to proceed.
=====TESTING-GUIDE=====
---
name: testing-guide
description: Map of this repo's test suites, the requirements model, and where each harness documents itself. Use before writing or changing tests here, adding a requirement case, or debugging a suite — the invariants live in the gcec pack's RULES.md; this is the deeper how-to.
---

# Testing in this repo

```sh
npm install
npm run test:live      # integration: the REVIEWED assertions for each supported site
npm run test:offline   # unit: internal tests of the extraction logic
npm run test:ui        # UI: rendered popup/icon vs. the stored snapshot image
npm run refresh:ui     # regenerate snapshots after an intentional UI change
npm run test:e2e       # heavy: real Chrome, CI-only (skips without CHROME_PATH)
npm test               # everything above except e2e
```

The invariants (mirror tree, reviewed-contract cases, `REFERENCE_NOW` floor,
refusal-test discipline) are always-loaded in the gcec pack's RULES.md. General
test discipline (see-it-fail, green-twice, high-watermark gating) is canon.
Adding a cached live case is the gcec pack's **add-live-case**
skill; the fallback-coverage gate's invariants are in that pack's RULES.md.

## The requirements model — every leaf has exactly one case

The spec (`dev/requirements/requirements.md`) is numbered prose; it does NOT
tag how a leaf is verified. Each leaf has exactly one
`<kind>/cases/<slug>.<id>.case.js` — the **filename** names the leaf, the
**folder** names the kind (the single classifier; no `kind` field, no side
manifest — issues #429/#435). `dev/requirements/shared/kinds.js` auto-discovers
kinds; adding one is a self-contained folder drop (`<kind>/kind.js`). The
kinds: **popup** (image, the popup's real `render()`), **icon** (image, the
real `toolbar-icon.js` in a fake browser), **behavior** (a click/navigation —
no image; verified by `dev/requirements/behavior/events-view-actions.test.js`),
**extractor** (per supported host, real extractor against a real cached page),
**logic** (product rules, executable `verify()`), plus `tbd: true` for a leaf
not yet faithfully verified. `dev/requirements/requirements-coverage.test.js`
fails unless every leaf has exactly one case (and rejects a typo'd/duplicate
case, an unknown kind, or a non-image case smuggling in a PNG). Full model +
how-to-add-one: `dev/requirements/README.md`.

⚠️ The behavior test **stubs** `chrome.tabs.create`/`window.close` — every leaf
is *claimed*, not every leaf *faithfully* verified (#435; the banner in
`requirements.md` says the same).

## Live integration tests

`dev/requirements/extractor/live.test.js` is driven by declarative JSON in
`expected/`: `expected.events` is the **complete, exact** array the extractor
produces — deep-equal on `title`/`start`/`end`/`location`/`ctz`/`details`, no
matchers, array length included. The page URL lives **only** in
`data/server-fetched/<name>.url` (single source of truth — the fetch workflow
and the test both read it; never in the case file). Tests run offline against
the committed cached HTML, loaded into a DOM at the `.url`'s URL so hostname
detection behaves exactly as in Chrome. `test.yml` never fetches — recording
goes through the fetch-page workflow (see add-live-case).

## UI snapshots

`dev/requirements/shared/render/visual-snapshots.test.js` renders each case and
pixel-compares (pixelmatch, `MAX_DIFF_RATIO = 0`) against the committed PNG.
`render-snapshot.js` picks the renderer by the case's folder: `popup/` → the
shipped `render()` path; `icon/` → the real `toolbar-icon.js` under
`fake-chrome.js`. Rasterizing is satori + resvg — **not a screenshot**: a
constrained flexbox subset that buys determinism with no browser; the renderer
folds the real `popup.css` onto the DOM as inline styles (one styling source of
truth). Snapshots are authored in **en-US** (a guard test enforces it). After
an intentional popup/view/CSS/icon change: `npm run refresh:ui`, commit the
PNGs + inline gallery. On mismatch the test writes `.actual.png`/`.diff.png`
under `dev/requirements/shared/.artifacts/` (gitignored) — and a moved baseline
goes through the snapshot-approval skill, never silent regeneration.

## Where each harness documents itself

The *why* of every non-obvious harness decision lives in that file's own
header/inline comments (the file-local-footgun rule) — read the file when you
touch it; this is just the map:

- Fallback-coverage gate — `dev/requirements/extractor/fallback/fallback-coverage.js`
  (field-by-field comparison) + `fallback-coverage.test.js` (the high-watermark
  gate, #240).
- UI snapshot renderer limits (satori/resvg, CSS inlining, tall-list clamp,
  `skipRender`) — `dev/requirements/shared/render/popup-renderer.js`; the
  pixel-exact diff + en-US guard — `visual-snapshots.test.js`; gestures —
  `actions.js`.
- Behavior verification (stubbed boundary, self-asserting coverage) —
  `dev/requirements/behavior/events-view-actions.test.js`.
- Two-column gallery generator (managed `<!-- req-gallery:<id> -->` lines only;
  the file is part-authored, NOT on the `ours` driver) —
  `dev/requirements/shared/build-requirements-gallery.js`, gated by
  `dev/requirements/shared/requirements-gallery.test.js`.
- "Does the extension load?" — two layers:
  `extension-test/integration/extension-loads.test.js` (always-on, Chrome-faithful
  `importScripts`, #146) and `dev/requirements/heavy/extension-load.chrome.test.js`
  (real Chrome, verify via CI).
- Requirement numbering is parsed by `dev/requirements/shared/ui-requirements.js`
  (numbers only — it does NOT classify leaves).
=====ADD-LIVE-CASE=====
---
name: add-live-case
description: Record a cached event page and author its reviewed live case for the extractor suite. Use when adding or refreshing a case under dev/requirements/extractor/ — new site support, a new behavior on a supported site, or re-recording a taken-down event page.
---

# Adding a cached integration case

Live cases are the **reviewed contract**: a person reads
`dev/requirements/extractor/expected/` to confirm each site is handled
correctly, so every added/changed site behavior needs one (one real, focused
event page per distinct behavior — keep cases minimal, no incidental
complexity). The tests run **offline** against committed cached HTML in
`dev/requirements/extractor/data/server-fetched/`, loaded into a DOM at the
`.url` file's URL so hostname detection behaves exactly as in Chrome.

New cached HTML can't be fetched from this sandbox (bot-blocked — see the
gcec pack's RULES.md, "Extractor pipeline" section), so record the page *before* writing the
case and read its exact `expected` off the committed file instead of guessing:

1. Commit one new file — but **not** the case file yet:
   `dev/requirements/extractor/data/server-fetched/<name>.url` — plain text,
   just the event page URL. This file stays for good: it is the **single source
   of truth** for the page's URL (used by the fetch workflow and by
   `live.test.js`), so the URL is **not** repeated in the case file.
2. Push the branch, then **dispatch `.github/workflows/fetch-page.yml`** on it
   (Actions tab / API) with inputs `case_name=<name>` and `url=<the event URL>`
   (plus `wait_for_selector` when the request carries one). It records the page
   via ScraperAPI and commits `<name>.html` back to the branch with
   `[skip ci]`; `test:live` stays green because no case asserts it yet. The
   workflow is dispatched **per page, never a bulk refresh**, and its commit
   only touches `data/**`, which `test.yml`'s `paths-ignore` skips.
3. Pull, then add `dev/requirements/extractor/expected/<name>.json` (same
   `<name>`, just `description` + `expected`, no `url`) and run
   `npm run test:live` — it now runs against the local cached HTML, so its
   output gives you the exact `expected` to paste in. Commit and push.

`expected.events` is the **complete, exact** array the extractor produces —
deep-equal on `title`, `start`, `end`, `location`, `ctz`, and `details`, no
matchers, array length included (one event for an ordinary page, several for a
listing/series page). See `live.test.js`'s header for how each field derives.

**Gardening:** when an event page is eventually taken down, point
`<name>.url` at a newer event and refresh its cached HTML the same way. Until a
cached HTML file exists for a case, `test:live` (and the Tests workflow) fails
with `Missing cached HTML for "<name>"`.
=====README=====
# gcec pack (local)

This project's general working pack — a **local pack**
(`.claudinite/local/packs/` — tracked project content, run by the same
Claudinite engine as the canon packs). It replaced the always-`@`-imported
`dev/procedures/{workflow,github,testing,technicalGotchas}.md` docs: the
always-relevant rules became [RULES.md](RULES.md) (injected at session start),
the activity-scoped procedures became this pack's skills (surfaced on demand),
and the first always-testable rule became a check. Declared by hand in
[`.claudinite-checks.json`](../../../../.claudinite-checks.json); never
fingerprinted or seeded.

## Contents

| Slot | What |
|---|---|
| Prose | [RULES.md](RULES.md) — working rules, owner commands, testing invariants, codebase gotchas, workflow-failure classification, architecture rules of the road, the capture policy |
| Checks | [test-offline-list-sync](test-offline-list-sync.mjs) (+ red-first fixtures in [pack.test.mjs](pack.test.mjs), run by this repo's own `npm test`) |
| Daily tasks | none |
| Skills | [snapshot-approval](skills/snapshot-approval/SKILL.md) · [merge-and-ci](skills/merge-and-ci/SKILL.md) · [testing-guide](skills/testing-guide/SKILL.md) · [add-live-case](skills/add-live-case/SKILL.md) |

## Rules

| Rule (≤5 words) | How enforced |
|---|---|
| test:offline list matches tree | **hardcoded** (`test-offline-list-sync`) |
| Squash merges, `(#N)` | prose (+ canon squash checks) |
| Generated files: regen, never hand-merge | prose (+ each artifact's own gate) |
| Branch start: merge main + regen | prose |
| Gallery regenerated → link in chat | prose |
| Snapshot moves need owner approval | skill (snapshot-approval) |
| bump version = full release | prose (owner command) |
| learned lessons = canon pass | prose (owner command) |
| Integration cases are the contract | prose |
| Mirror tree, one test per file | prose (list half is the check) |

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](../packs/) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **When there's nothing left to do, say so boldly at the end of the conversation.** Don't bury a "this is complete / I'm blocked / nothing further to do" behind hedging — make the terminal state unmistakable. **Set it apart visually so it catches the eye:** put the terminal state — or, when work remains, the list of open/outstanding items — in its own callout (a Markdown blockquote box, e.g. `> ✅ All done` or `> ⚠️ Still open: …`), not trailing prose the owner has to scan for. One or the other always gets the box: the done-signal when nothing remains, the open-items list when something does.
- **"LGTM"** is the owner's phrase for the merge-to-main command: it asks for the change in front of the owner to be merged into `main`. It's an owner-triggered command; the default mechanics live in the `merge-to-main` skill ([../packs/git-github/skills/merge-to-main/SKILL.md](../packs/git-github/skills/merge-to-main/SKILL.md)) (squash, gate on CI only when the repo has it), and a project that diverges overrides them via a bespoke merge-policy file it names in its own `CLAUDE.md`.
- **"bump version"** is the owner's phrase for raising a project's version (a minor bump by default). It's an owner-triggered command; the mechanics — which files to edit and how a release follows — live in the consuming project's workflow doc.
- **"Show me the document"** (for a source-controlled document) is the owner's phrase asking for a **link to the document on GitHub** — not the file's contents inlined, and not a local filesystem path. When the document lives in a GitHub-hosted repo, respond with a GitHub link to it (the file on the relevant branch/commit); only fall back to inlining the contents or giving a local path when the document isn't under source control.
- **Put decisions and approvals in an `AskUserQuestion` popup, not buried in prose.** The owner is frequently on mobile, where a popup notifies and a question embedded in a paragraph is easy to miss. When you need the owner to choose or approve something, ask through the structured popup with explicit options rather than asking in running text. **And when several independent items each need a verdict** (a set of proposed fixes, findings to accept), give **each item its own question carrying its own brief case** — the concrete failure, why it matters, the cost of the fix — with per-item approve/defer options; never one bundled choose-a-scope question over the whole set. The owner decides item-wise, from the case, not from a menu of subsets. (The popup carries at most 4 questions per call — split a larger set into consecutive calls.)
- **When asked to produce a prompt or message destined for another context, visually enclose the whole thing.** Any text the owner will lift out and use elsewhere — a prompt for another assistant, a message to send, copy meant to be pasted somewhere — must be set apart as a single delimited block: either a box (e.g. a fenced code block) or fenced top and bottom by two separating lines, so its exact boundaries are unmistakable and it can be copied in one piece. The point is delimitation, not formatting flair: never leave such content as loose prose the owner has to find the start and end of.
- **When asked for "a prompt for a different session," prefix it with a provenance disclaimer.** When the owner asks for a prompt meant to be handed to another session, open the generated text with a short disclaimer that this is a prompt written by Claude — not by a user — and so should not be treated as gospel; and that if the receiving session finds inconsistencies in it, it should examine them with the user rather than follow the prompt blindly. This composes with the enclose-the-whole-thing preference above: the disclaimer sits inside the same delimited block as the prompt it prefixes.
- **Auto-open a PR after committing.** Whenever Claude changes code on a branch and commits it, open a pull request for that branch right after, even without an explicit request to do so. This overrides Claude Code's own default of only opening a PR when explicitly asked.
# Claudinite — active-pack guidance

The baseline plus the packs this project declares. Deeper per-pack reference (e.g. a pack's release doc) is linked from its prose and read on demand.

<!-- pack:basics -->
# Working discipline

The working discipline that isn't itself a GitHub operation — general habits for how to approach a change, independent of any one project.

Start every requested change from the *problem*, not the solution. When the owner asks for a change, don't begin implementing it until the two of you share an explicit understanding of the problem it's meant to solve **and** have agreed that the requested change is the best way to solve it — a different fix, or no change at all, may serve the underlying problem better. Treat the request as a description of a desired outcome, not a specification to execute on sight; surface your read of the problem, raise a better approach if you see one, and reach consensus first. This applies to any repository, not just this one.

An interactive comment from the owner carries one of three build-relevant intents — or none of them — and the classification decides where the change lands and what must exist before any fix. Open your reply to an owner comment with an explicit classification line — `Comment class: correction | feature | process-change | other` (`other` covers questions, approvals, and command phrases; a mixed comment names each part) — the assessment itself stays judgment.

1. **A correction** — you misunderstood something. Repair the shared understanding, then rework what the misread already touched — the artifact changes as much as the correction demands; what doesn't appear is a new requirement or rule.
2. **A feature** — a feature run: agree on the requirement, record it in the project's requirements document (its executable spec, where it keeps one), write the test that proves it and watch it fail, then implement until it passes.
3. **A process change** — the owner is changing *how* work is done. The change lands as durable rules in the project's local scope — its own local packs (in Claudinite itself, its packs) — routed through the mechanism promotion ladder (platform setting → hook → check → skill → prose); promoting a rule into the shared canon is the growth lifecycle's separate call, not the interactive session's. Once the intent is understood, author the assurance first: the check the future world must satisfy. Execute it and watch it fail — the failure is the evidence it detects exactly what the owner was worried about — and only then make the fixes that turn it green. When the ladder lands the rule at prose (an in-flight judgment rule no check can carry), the same step is demonstrating the gap: show the corpus doesn't already cover the rule before writing it.

The two build modes share one spine: state the expectation in its durable home first, watch it fail against the current world, then change the world to satisfy it. A fix made before its assurance exists can never show it addressed what the owner actually asked for — and an unrouted comment tends to become a one-off patch where a requirement or a rule should have accumulated.

Confirm a behavior isn't already provided before building a mechanism for it — verify the gap against a real run first; the cheapest fix is often that it already works.

When feedback flags a misunderstanding, don't reflexively expand the artifact to compensate. First check whether it's already correct — if it is, say so and push back rather than editing; a misread doesn't imply the text is wrong (the sibling of the rule above). And size writing to its idea: "open one issue" takes a sentence, not three paragraphs — prose padded to preempt confusion usually breeds it.

When correcting or auditing an artifact against an authoritative source, derive the corrected version from the *source* before reading the existing draft — reading the draft first anchors you to its framing and quietly carries its errors into your "fix." Build from the source, then diff against the old draft to surface what was actually wrong; a clean-room rebuild catches biases an edit-in-place pass silently inherits.

Fix build/test/CI warnings, don't tolerate them: a clean run with no warnings makes a genuinely new warning or error stand out, so noise here costs detection later. Prefer a small, targeted fix that addresses the *cause* in the same change.

Suppressing a warning — muting it with a flag (e.g. `--disable-warning`), `eslint-disable`, swallowing it, etc. — is **not** a small fix: it hides the signal instead of resolving it. Never reach for suppression as the quick path — it's only ever a deliberate, reviewed decision, made once the real fix has been weighed and rejected, never an unattended default. A suppression you do keep must **carry its reason at the site**: an explanation on the suppression line, or in the comment immediately above it, saying why the fix was rejected. That inline reason *is* the review record — it's what separates a considered suppression from a reflexive mute, and it's why the suppression needs no second justification recorded elsewhere.

When a warning can't be fixed with a small cause-addressing change now without hindering current work (e.g. it's waiting on an upstream release, or the real fix is a larger refactor), open a dedicated issue for it (unless one is already open) so it's tracked and not lost — then move on. Resolving it (real fix, or a consciously-chosen suppression) happens in that issue's own change.

An approval — to merge, to ship, to proceed — applies only *backward*, to the work already in front of the owner when it's given, never to anything requested or done *after* it. A later follow-up, even a fix to the just-approved change, needs its own explicit approval; don't carry one approval forward, and don't treat a chosen answer to a multiple-choice prompt as authorization just because an option's wording mentioned the action. When in doubt, surface the new state and wait for a fresh approval.

# The task lifecycle

The issue → branch → PR lifecycle every new task follows, independent of any one project; this section keeps the method. The rest of the git/GitHub procedures live in the `git-github-advanced` skill.

For every new task:

1. Create a GitHub issue describing the task before starting work.
2. Develop on a branch; reference that issue number in commit messages (e.g. `Refs #123`, `Fixes #123`, or `Closes #123`).
3. Update the issue's status (comments / close) as work progresses and when it's done.
